children: Oil futures are steady in early U.S. trading, with WTI for December delivery making its debut at the front of the curve. Yesterday's high of $110 a barrel for the expiring November contract "provides an eventual upside target to WTI when looking across the next 1-2-week time frame," Ritterbusch & Associates says in a note. The firm cautions against chasing WTI higher above $102 "since the bulk of the past week's upside price acceleration appears attributable to increased risk appetite rather than a shift in global crude balances." December WTI is off 0.1% at $97.72 a barrel and Brent is down 0.3% at $108.51 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
